title.en: Forced World Refreshes Will Be Significantly Reduced for WoW: Forever
title.es: Las actualizaciones forzosas del mundo se reducirán significativamente para WoW: Forever

summary.en: Forced World Refreshes Will Be Significantly Reduced for WoW: Forever...
summary.es: Las actualizaciones forzosas del mundo se reducirán significativamente para WoW: Forever...

contentHtml:
On WoW: Forever's launch, joining a group won't automatically phase you anymore, and forced layer refreshes shouldn't happen as often.

In the latest episode of the WoW: Forever podcast, Principal Software Engineer Frank Williams discusses forced layering and lessons from the Beta. WoW: Forever features new layering technology because the game no longer has any realms. He describes how the system is designed to put players on a partition of the world where it thinks their community is: whether that's players you might recognize or allied (or enemy) guilds. The goal is to have consistency and repeated interactions, and for players to see the same people while leveling, because then you might decide to do a dungeon with them or join their guild.

On the Beta, many players noticed there was a new pop-up when you were scheduled to get layered. In addition, this happened a lot at the start of the beta, and Frank Williams noted that their algorithms were overaggressive and trying too hard to make sure everyone was with their community.


Source: WoW: Forever Podcast Episode 6


At the start of the Beta, players were getting moved around a lot, and this graph shows the number of times that the popup showed up for players. As they started fixing and tuning things, they got to the point where the system wasn't moving players around as much. After the first two weeks and some fine-tuning, they realized the system was working, and he mentions how they don't have to force the community. He continues to discuss how the system will change launch, particularly when grouping with other players.
Frank Williams said:
Now the philosophy of how that pop-up works is generally you're not going to get moved. It's going to pop up in a more limited capacity and be much more friendly. One change you're going to notice at launch is that when you join a group, it's actually going to just do that pop-up; it's not going to just move you. Because I think universally we want it to be consistent, where we're not going to disrupt your gameplay, and when Hardcore comes out, shortly, that's going to be a huge thing. You don't want to be in a cave, and oops, you got moved to a spot where there's an Elite standing right next to you. Now you're going to have a time window.
On the Beta and on Retail, players are automatically phased when you join a group. This should no longer be the case on WoW: Forever, and players will have the option of when to make the change, within a certain time limit.

This new layering system should allow for more repeated interactions with particular players and guilds. From the Beta, they feel like they've dialed things to the appropriate levels, and on launch, you can expect something that feels like the flow of Classic.

title.en: Return to Azeroth Recap for World of Warcraft: Forever
title.es: Resumen de Regreso a Azeroth para World of Warcraft: Forever

summary.en: Return to Azeroth Recap for World of Warcraft: Forever...
summary.es: Regreso a Azeroth Recapitulación de World of Warcraft: Forever...

contentHtml:
Blizzard reminds players about what awaits them when they return to Azeroth on November 4th for World of Warcraft: Forever.
Blizzard
View Original
World of Warcraft: Forever begins a new journey through a reimagined original world, with new zones, quests, dungeons, systems, and character options designed to expand the adventure while preserving its foundational character. If you’re returning to Azeroth, we’ve got what you need to get you started on your path.

Where Your Story Begins

WoW: Forever begins in the early “Year 1” period of original World of Warcraft, before Kazzak reopened the Dark Portal and before later journeys to places like Northrend reshaped the timeline. The game is built from the original level 1–60 world, expanding events, characters, and locations that exist—or could have existed—within that foundational era. This opens up new opportunities to delve into previously undeveloped areas, experience new tales, and travel roads yet untaken.

Discover What Awaits in WoW: Forever

Explore New and Reimagined Lands

WoW: Forever expands the Eastern Kingdoms and Kalimdor with new and reimagined zones and more than 1,000 new quests across the level 1–60 journey. Explore new destinations including Mount Hyjal, Shen’dralas, the Riverglades, and Zephras Isle.

Brave Nine New Dungeons

Nine new five-player dungeons span levels 13–60 across the Eastern Kingdoms and Kalimdor. Each adds new threats, quests, and stories rooted in the original world.
  • Eastern Kingdoms: Hall of Thanes, Ruins of Lordaeron, Excavation Site, City of Dalaran, The Drowned City, and Krol’dok Stronghold.
  • Kalimdor: Alcaz Prison, Blackmaw Hold, and Shaper’s Terrace.
Read the previously published dungeon overview for locations, level ranges, access notes, and story details.

New Class and Race Combinations

Your favorite race or class may still be waiting for you, but WoW: Forever also opens combinations that were not available in original World of Warcraft:
  • Alliance: Human Hunter, Dwarf Shaman, and Gnome Priest.
  • Horde: Orc Mage, Troll Warlock, and Undead Paladin.
The Skyborne race adds more choices. This new playable race can join either the Alliance or the Horde at character creation, with unique racial abilities depending on that choice, and begins in the level 1–12 Zephras Isle starting zone. Skyborne can be Druids, Hunters, Rogues, and Warriors; Alliance-aligned Skyborne can also be Mages, while Horde-aligned Skyborne can also be Shaman. Skyborne access requires the purchase of the Heroic Pack or higher digital upgrades.

Make Every Part of the Journey Count with the Legacy System

World of Warcraft: Forever introduces an exciting new account-wide horizontal progression system—the Legacy System. It’s a whole new way to progress, focusing on exploring everything the game has to offer, rather than power progression alone.

This new system encourages players to level multiple characters of different classes and tradeskills and experience the journey all over again, however leveling alternate (alts) characters is not required to benefit from the system. All character advantages can be unlocked on a single character. Take a closer look in our previously published article.

Progress Through the Updated PvP System

Whether you’re charging into battlegrounds with your faction or setting your sights on long-term PvP goals, World of Warcraft: Forever brings a refreshed sense of purpose to every match-up. Players earn Honor and Rank points through battlegrounds, PvP quests, weekly seasonal tasks, and other PvP activities; battleground holiday weeks provide additional gains.

Learn more in our previously published PvP progression overview.

Battle for the Darkspear Islands

Darkspear Islands is a new 15 versus 15 battleground off the coast of Dustwallow Marsh for levels 30–60. Teams earn points by controlling four capture points and securing a central flag; the first team reaching 2,000 points wins.

Players can build reputation with the Darkspear Raiders or Theramore Expeditionary Force to unlock faction rewards. Read the previously published Darkspear Islands battleground overview for more information.

See Azeroth the Way You Remember It

The first time you log in to World of Warcraft: Forever, you’ll be asked to Choose Your Experience Preset. You’ll make this choice before selecting your Ruleset.
You can change the selection later or fine-tune your experience in the Options Menu under System – Preset. After your initial log in to the game, you will no longer see this screen.

Each time you create a new character, you can select either High Definition (HD) or Standard Definition (SD) character models and animations. HD uses higher-detail models and updated visuals, while SD offers the style associated with the original look of World of Warcraft. This character-specific choice affects only appearance—not abilities or progression—and you can change it later in the Options Menu or by visiting a Barbershop in game.

Make a Name for Yourself—Twice

In WoW: Forever, every character has a two-part name, similar to a first name and surname. The complete combination must be unique within your region, giving you more room to carry forward a favorite name or build a new identity.
  • Use the second name to build identity. It can suggest a family, place, reputation, title, guild theme, or connection among alternate characters.
  • Follow the naming policy. Both parts are evaluated together and must comply with the in-game Code of Conduct.
  • Have a backup. Full-name combinations are claimed on a first-come, first-served basis.
  • Adjust how it appears. You can hide your secondary name above your character through Nameplates options, although it still appears in chat.
Learn more in the previously published character-naming overview.

Choose How You Want to Experience Azeroth

Instead of choosing from a long list of realms, players select a Ruleset that matches how they want to experience Azeroth. Each Ruleset operates as its own large ecosystem for grouping, dungeons, raids, and community.
  • Normal: Focus on adventuring and fighting monsters, with player-versus-player combat available at your discretion.
  • PvP: Focus on player-versus-player combat, with the risk of being attacked by opposing players through much of the open world.
  • Roleplay: Enter a community with naming and behavior rules intended for players who want to immerse themselves as characters in a fantasy world.
  • Roleplay-PvP: Join an immersive roleplaying community while also facing the danger of open-world conflict with the opposing faction.
  • Hardcore (coming later): Take on a high-stakes challenge where every decision matters and a character’s journey can end with death. Additional details and timing will be shared later.
Make sure you coordinate with your friends and guild before creating your character to play in the same Ruleset and faction to group, run dungeons, and raid together. Review our previously published Ruleset overview before organizing a guild or friend group.

Prepare Your PC for the Journey

Before installing, update your operating system and graphics drivers, then review the official system requirements for WoW: Forever.

Returning to Azeroth with Account Recovery

If you cannot sign in, Blizzard Support offers account-recovery options for locating an account, resetting a password, unlocking access, addressing authenticator issues, and recovering an account when you no longer have access to its email address.
  1. Start with “Can’t Log In?” Use the account recovery page to locate the account, reset a password, unlock access, or address authenticator issues.
  2. Secure a compromised account. If you suspect the account was hacked, secure your computer and email account, request restoration, change your password, and add a Battle.net Authenticator..
  3. Ask for additional help. If self-service options do not resolve the issue, use the Blizzard Support portal to contact a Game Master.
  4. Confirm your WoW account. After recovering access, verify the region, license, contact details, and security settings you want to use for WoW: Forever.

Install Battle.net to Get Started

  1. Download the Battle.net desktop app for Windows or Mac and log in to your account.
  2. Open the Battle.net desktop app and select WoW: Forever from the menu.
  3. Under the Game Version menu, select WoW: Forever. You'll see a second dropdown for each account if you have more than one World of Warcraft account. Select the active account you wish to play on from that column.
  4. Click the Install button. The progress bar will show you when the game is available to play.
  5. Once the installation is complete, click the Play button.

Subscription or Game Time Is Required

Access to WoW: Forever is included with an active World of Warcraft subscription or Game Time. Optional upgrade editions include cosmetics and other benefits; access to the Skyborne race and starting experience requires the Skyborne Heroic Pack or higher.

Carve Your Path

Gather your friends, choose the character and ruleset that fit how you want to play, and begin your journey in World of Warcraft: Forever. Welcome back, adventurers!

title.en: Blizzard Working on Top Layering Issues in WoW: Forever
title.es: Blizzard trabaja en los principales problemas de capas en WoW: Forever

summary.en: Blizzard Working on Top Layering Issues in WoW: Forever...
summary.es: Blizzard trabaja en los principales problemas de capas en WoW: Forever...

contentHtml:
In the latest episode of the WoW: Forever Podcast, Blizzard has addressed that they are working on the most noticeable layer issues players saw on the Beta.

Layering and Large Scale PvP

In the WoW: Forever Beta, players tested the limits of how much a layer could handle. Large-scale world PvP battles were tested, and while some were successful, others found themselves struggling to get everyone on the same layer. This week's guest on the podcast, Shobek, asked if there was anything to adjust to help with these large-scale battles.
Aggrend said:
"There's a lot of cool things people are doing, using addons and stuff to organize things; we look at a lot of that functionality really closely and say, hey, what do we really wanna pull and try to integrate?"
Featured developer on this week's podcast episode, Principal Software Engineer Frank Williams, would also share that they do have something on the board later down the line to maybe try and help with world PvP battles happening on a grand scale.
"There might be a whiteboard on campus with the word "megaraid" scrawled on it, but we've also been thinking of ways to auto-detect PvP battles that are happening and have the servers expand slightly to keep the battle continuous and flowing. But I would say the state at the end of the beta is what you can expect for launch."

Layering between zones

A more common issue amongst players, however, is layering that occurs between each zone. Alliance players might be following a herd of their peers from Hillsbrad Foothills into Silverpine Forest as they make their way to Shadowfang Keep, but as soon as they cross the barrier from zone to zone, you could see a large number of these players disappear as they've now entered new layers.
Aggrend said:
"One of the things we can kind of tune or tweak are which zones are actually connected to each other. That's why you're in Durotar watching people duel, and then someone suddenly appears out of nowhere because they walked out of Orgrimmar... for launch, that's an important thing to have because Durotar will be slammed, whereas there won't be many people idling in Orgrimmar; however, later on, it'll flip. We can fine-tune when we group things so at launch, the way it looks may be much different than the way it looks a month down the road."
Frank Williams also stated that layering features like that were already adjusted in the final couple of days of the beta and the stress test, and that more improvements and tweaks are in the works, but it's just the tradeoff of how Forever is designed. Although the design isn't perfect, as they've stated in the podcast, they said that you still will see zone layering happen, but they are looking at the best possible ways to make this system work in the long run.

title.en: WoW: Forever is Aiming for a 4-Month Patch Cadence
title.es: WoW: Forever apunta a una cadencia de parches de 4 meses

summary.en: WoW: Forever is Aiming for a 4-Month Patch Cadence...
summary.es: WoW: Forever apunta a una cadencia de parches de 4 meses...

contentHtml:
In an interview with IGN, Kris Zierhut announced that they are looking at a 4-month patch cadence for WoW: Forever.

IGN WoW: Forever Interview


IGN asked Blizzard in an interview about the patch cadence of WoW: Forever. Kris Zierhut, Principal Game Designer, commented that they have experimented a lot with the Patch cadence throughout Classic, and with SoD, they did a patch every eight to ten weeks, which felt way too fast. They believe that the correct release cadence for patches is about one every 4 months or 17 weeks.
Kris Zierhut said:
And then one nuance on that is we do plan on making content that unlocks in between. So you might have patches with major releases four months apart, but there may be things that unlock two or three months in or one month into that.
Since they're focusing on smaller, more local stories, they believe that 4 months is an appropriate amount of development time. PvP Seasons will also match this and last for 4 months. However, he mentions that additional things might unlock within the major 4-month patches. The patch won't launch with everything released, but things will slowly unlock over 4 months to give things more of a lifespan.

title.en: Patch Cadence, Future Locations, Respeccing - IGN Interview on WoW: Forever
title.es: Cadencia de parches, ubicaciones futuras, respeto - Entrevista de IGN en WoW: Forever

summary.en: Patch Cadence, Future Locations, Respeccing - IGN Interview on WoW: Forever...
summary.es: Cadencia de parches, ubicaciones futuras, respeto - Entrevista de IGN en WoW: Forever...

contentHtml:
IGN interviewed Blizzard on WoW: Forever and discussed the patch cadence, locations for future patches, respeccing, and a lot more!

IGN WoW: Forever Interview


IGN interviewed the following team members on WoW: Forever:
  • Kris Zierhut, Principal Game Designer
  • Tim Jones, Lead Classic Designer

Interview Summary

Different Games
  • WoW Classic is similar to a museum. It's been that way for years with very little change. They can preserve that for people who want to see what it was like.
  • WoW: Forever is their take on what they could do if they never went to Outland and kept developing the world, whether that's adding new quests or Professions.
Choosing What Changes
  • When choosing what to change from WoW: Classic, they look at their four main pillars. The most important is likely "the world is the main character".
  • The Journey should be as important as the destination, and the world should feel full, no matter what zone you go to.
  • They loved how in Hardcore, it always felt like every zone was filled with other players; likely because players had to reroll whenever they died.
  • For "approachable and familiar", they feel that the base classic game is approachable, and they've taken careful consideration with familiar things like SD models.
  • Regarding the UI, while they're using a lot of modern UI conveniences, it still feels like a Classic game and not a copy of the retail UI.
  • They've also worked on "unsolving" the game so players don't have the perfect leveling path or profession choices.
Lightning and Shadow Improvements
  • People remember WoW in 2004 a lot better than it actually was, so they wanted to give players Azeroth as they remember it, not as it actually was.
  • They want to drive new players into the game. They want to bring in the next generation of gamers who are used to a lot of high graphic fidelity.
WoW Engine
  • The WoW engine is not spaghetti code. That's an unfair player characterization.
  • Kris Zierhut has heard many other devs comment that they want the WoW engine.
  • Developers have worked hard over the last 25 years to improve the engine, get a higher frame rate, and improve server response times.
Release Cadence
  • They've experimented a lot with release cadence throughout Classic.
  • They know that going without new content for six to eight weeks feels bad.
  • For SoD, they went to an eight- to ten-week schedule, and it felt too fast.
  • They believe that the correct update cadence is about once every 4 months or 3 times a year.
  • This is one of the advantages of telling smaller, more localized stories. They don't need 6 months to tell the giant huge story.
  • They come up with enough stories to fill a 4-month development period.
  • They do plan on having content in between, so there might be content that unlocks between that.
Places to Go
  • There are 3 types of content. First is the path you know: Molten Core, Blackwing Lair, and AQ. Forever will go there, but they're stretching out the timeline a bit.
  • There are places that are new that feel like they belong, such as the Riverglades. Some future dungeons and raids will fit here as well.
  • Then they can go out of their way to do something very different, such as the Skyborne and Zephras Isle.
  • The Dark Portal, Northrend, and Pandaria all exist, and they could make minor adventures in those areas, such as a dungeon or quest that takes you there and then comes back. They won't be doing this soon, and when they do, you will always come home to the Eastern Kingdoms and Kalimdor.
Player Housing
  • They don't have plans to add player housing to Forever right now.
Horizontal Progression and Raids
  • They're aware there will be a point when there are too many raids and dungeons, and they don't know how to solve that yet.
  • They're thinking about how to solve it, with many plans and ideas, but right now they're focused on shipping the game.
Respeccing Talents
  • Dual spec is available at launch, and a third spec is not off the table for the future.
  • They do not want you to be able to change your talents on the fly, as this creates an expectation that you will change your talents for every encounter, and that isn't approachable and familiar.
  • They have been talking about making it easier to change your talent specs when you need it.
Griefing
  • Griefing is a problem that is part of gaming, and it is their duty to make a game that pushes people towards positive social interactions, and not pushing people towards toxic interactions.
  • They're doing a lot of things that they call pro-social design, such as the camping system or elite zone quests.
  • They also have 4 different group sizes: 5, 10, 20, and 40. If you don't have enough people, you might remember a good social experience you had and invite them to get the required numbers.
  • The more resilient and positive a social network, the less likely there are for players to be jerks.
Hyjal
  • Hyjal looks very different in Forever, as there is no flying and players are forced to view it from the ground.
  • There are callouts to the Mount Hyjal raid that players will see.
Other Locations
  • They want to go to the Emerald Dream.
  • They also want to go to Grim Batol, not like a dungeon, but as a place you explore like Blackrock Mountain.
  • There are definitely places in the Caverns of Time that they haven't explored.
  • Gilneas is on the map, but is inaccessible right now. There will be a whole story there to explore before it gets destroyed in the Cataclysm.
  • They would like to get to Silvermoon eventually, but as it's currently the focus of Retail, they would rather focus elsewhere for the time being.
Skyborne
  • Elves are the most popular races in WoW
  • The current races from Vanilla tend to cause a population imbalance. A lot of players don't want to be "a monster".
Downtime
  • There will definitely be downtime when you can play both games.
  • Retail is focused on max-level gameplay, and that comes in bursts, so between that you might play some WoW: Forever!
